platforms.price_note: Telegram-bot and API orders start from 1.1 TRX per hour (member pricing); the board shows the plain-transfer price. Pay-per-transfer mode: 2,2 TRX per USDT transfer.
platforms.terms_source: API docs enumerate the rental period as 1/24/72/168/336/720 hours (1h, 1d, 3d, 7d, 14d, 30d) and the published price table runs 1 Hour / 24 Hour / 72 Hour / 7 Day / 14 Day / 30 Day — no sub-hour period and no 240-hour one: apitrx.com/en/pages/energy.html
platforms.deal_model_source: Their order endpoint takes no price at all - only apikey, address, energy value and hours - and a separate endpoint publishes the rate per term: web.apitrx.com/price
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Their Chinese-language partner page invites TRX holders to sublet energy, but they publish no addresses, rates or delegation figures, so we do not state it.

platforms.terms_source: Their price endpoint quotes durations 1h and whole days 1-30 and answers '15min' with 'Duration must be a number of days (max. 14), 1h for 1 hour rental': dapp.brutus.finance
platforms.deal_model_source: Their order API quotes the price you pay: POST e-bot.brutusservices.com/main/prices returns {"response":1,"price":"3.12"} for a stated amount and duration
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Their API shows stock per rental term but says nothing about where that stock comes from.

platforms.deal_model_source: A flat published rate - "Each 3 TRX = 65,000 energy" - and their order method carries quantity, duration and receiver but no price field: docs.catfee.io/en/getting-started/quickstart
platforms.energy_source_source: They run an open vault for TRX holders - "Your TRX remains in your wallet. Only your generated Energy/Bandwidth is delegated" - and settle to them on-chain every 24 hours: docs.catfee.io/en/staking-vault/user-guide

platforms.price_note: EnergyFather's API documents six rental periods: one hour, and 1, 3, 7, 15 and 30 days. Ten days is not one of them. Their public price endpoint quotes the hourly rate only, and their order form shows a visitor no day option, so the hour is the one term the board can price here. We read it from the public endpoint they asked us to use, and it returns the same number an order would.
platforms.terms_source: Their API documentation states: 'Currently, only 6 periods are valid: 1 hour and 1, 3, 7, 15, 30 days.' Ten days is not one of them: energyfather.com/docs/api/v1/documentation
platforms.deal_model_source: Their own FAQ: "Rental price at EnergyFather does not change depending on the time of day or anything else", and the buy endpoint returns the cost rather than accepting one: energyfather.com/faq/buying-energy-faq
platforms.energy_source_source: They publish seller terms and a payout scheme, accepting sellers from 65,000 energy upward: energyfather.com/sell-tron-energy

platforms.price_note: Ergon quotes a tiered TRX per 1M energy PER DAY rate; the published price is rate x days x energy / 1e6. Rentals run 1-7d, so 15m/1h and 10d are not offered. The refundable 1-day security deposit is not included. Their order form takes any amount you type in, above a 100,000 floor; the 100,000 / 500,000 / 1,000,000 / 2,000,000 buttons beside it only fill the field. So both of the board's volumes are the same per-million rate, pro rata, and only the 65k one is under their minimum.
platforms.deal_model_source: Rentals run through a contract with a refundable deposit worth one day's rent, and the rate comes from a public method rather than from the buyer: ergon.ustx.io/php/ergonGetPrice.php
platforms.energy_source_source: The rentable pool is the contract's own, filled by depositors who get a liquid ERG token back - so the energy comes from one pool, not from many separate sellers: ergon.ustx.io

platforms.price_note: Feee.io answers only to addresses on their API whitelist, and the machine that reads this board is not on it right now. That is between us and their dashboard, and says nothing about the platform's own prices.
platforms.terms_source: Feee.io quoted all four terms to us directly, hundreds of times each, before their API stopped answering our address: feee.io
platforms.deal_model_source: Their C2C mode asks the buyer for "the energy unit price (a higher unit price can complete the transaction faster)" and fills when a seller takes the order. They also run a fixed-price instant mode beside it: feee.io
platforms.energy_source_source: Their C2C market is sellers taking buyer orders; the platform matches rather than supplies: feee.io

platforms.terms_source: Their own rental-period list reads 1 hour, 3 hours, 24 hours, 3 days, 1 week, 1 month — it starts at 15 min and never reaches ten days: feesaver.com/en
platforms.deal_model_source: Their purchase method takes token, days, volume and wallet - no price - and returns the cost it calculated: feesaver.com
platforms.energy_source_source: They publish terms for resource providers and settle to them: feesaver.com

platforms.terms_source: The Quick Rent form offers exactly four durations — 1H, 1D, 3D, 30D — so it steps straight from three days to thirty: itrx.io/en
platforms.deal_model_source: A keyless endpoint publishes the whole tier table - tiered_pricing with a price per period - and the order form has no price field: itrx.io/api/v1/frontend/index-data
platforms.energy_source_source: Their public data exposes per-term collection addresses and a delegating account fed by outside stakers: itrx.io/api/v1/frontend/index-data

platforms.price_note: JustLend DAO is a protocol, not a shop, and it charges in two parts: rent for the time you hold the energy, plus whatever it keeps from the security deposit for energy that has not grown back yet - up to three quarters of a day's rent, and nothing once a full day has passed. These prices are both parts, on the assumption that you spend the energy at the start of the rental and close the rental at the end of it, worked out with JustLend's own published formula and its own live rate. A rental also locks a refundable 20 TRX liquidation deposit, which comes back if you close the rental before it expires and is forfeited if you let it run out.
platforms.terms_source: JustLend DAO's own docs: energy is rented 'by the hour or by the day, with a maximum single rental period of 30 days': docs.justlend.org
platforms.deal_model_source: Renting here is delegation against refundable deposits, priced by a published formula on a public contract, not by a shop price: docs.justlend.org/developers/energy_rental
platforms.energy_source_source: One pool, readable on chain: totalDelegatedOfType(1) stands at about 335 million TRX against a maxRentableOfType of 4.49 billion on the rental contract TU2MJ5Veik1LRAgjeSzEdvmDYx7mefJZvd

platforms.price_note: MeFree sells whole transfers: 3 TRX buys 65,000 energy for one hour, and larger amounts are whole multiples of that. The same form quotes a different number in English and Russian: 5 TRX for the same transfer. We show the 3 because that is what mefree.net serves everyone by default, whatever language their browser asks for. Longer rentals exist through their API, which takes periods of 1 hour and 1 to 30 days, but its day rate is set per account rather than published, so the day columns here are the board's estimate.
platforms.terms_source: Their order API documents period as 0 = fast charge, 1 = one hour, 2 = 1 day, 3 = 3 days, and 4 to 30 = that many days: docs.mefree.net/api/create-order
platforms.deal_model_source: One announced rate per transfer in their own order form: <option value="3">3 TRX / 1 hour</option> at mefree.net
platforms.energy_source_unknown: They advertise a large energy pool but publish no address, contract or delegation figure to back it.

platforms.price_note: NETTS sells by the hour and by the day, up to 30 days, but the only price it publishes outside its own interface is the hourly one. The hour here is their number; the day columns are the board's estimate, because their day rate is quoted only inside their own order form.
platforms.terms_source: The duration selector on their own order form lists 1 hour and every whole day from 1 to 30, ten days included (<option value="864000">10 days</option>): netts.io
platforms.deal_model_source: They quote one rate to everyone through their own price feed and the buyer names nothing: netts.io/api/get-current-prices.php
platforms.energy_source_source: Their own homepage: "#1 energy aggregator pooling billions of energy units from verified providers including JustLend, Trongas, Catfee, Sohu, APITRX and private pools": netts.io

platforms.deal_model_source: Their published API calculates the cost for you - /precountOrder takes token, days and volume and returns the price: api.refee.bot/docs
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Their own site is behind a browser check we do not bypass, so we could not read anything about their supply.

platforms.terms_source: RentTron sells one product and states its length itself: 'Receive energy instantly upon TRX payment confirmation for 1 hour': renttron.com/en
platforms.deal_model_source: A keyless endpoint publishes the rate and the order method takes only addresses and amounts: renttron.com/api/prices
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Nothing on their site or in their API describes where their energy is staked or who supplies it.

platforms.terms_source: Their own wording: 'Flexible duration options: 15m, 1h, and 1d' — the list ends at one day: tofee.net
platforms.deal_model_source: A flat published rate you send to a deposit address - "Send 3.0 TRX per 65k Energy" for one hour - with no price field anywhere in the flow: tofee.net
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Their interface and API documentation point at TronMax, but whether they resell it or share an operator is not something we could establish.

platforms.terms_source: Their order form offers 15 minutes, 60 minutes, 24 hours and 72 hours (plus a renewing 72 hours); nothing longer: tr.energy/en
platforms.deal_model_source: Their API publishes period_prices_energy and the order body carries no price field at all, only amount and period: tr.energy
platforms.energy_source_source: Their own page for stakers: "You stake TRON - We sell the energy", and "Your funds are not transferred anywhere and remain on your wallet": tr.energy/en/stakers

platforms.price_note: TronEnergize is an order book, so this is the lowest price it will accept, not a posted rate: a seller still has to take the order. Their ladder of rental terms is 5 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours, 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days, so the board's 15-minute and 10-day columns have nothing to fill them.
platforms.terms_source: Their own price feed lists exactly eight rental terms, as durations in 3-second blocks: 5 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours, 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days (tronenergize.com/api/v1/minprices). Fifteen minutes and ten days are not among them.
platforms.deal_model_source: Every order in their public book carries the seller's stake and the APY he earns for filling it, and their price feed is named minprices — a floor the buyer has to clear, not a posted rate: tronenergize.com/api/v1/market
platforms.energy_source_source: The fourteen live orders in their public book name fourteen different receiver addresses, each with its own stake and APY, and sellers report their own delegation transactions through a separate endpoint: tronenergize.com/api/v1/market

platforms.price_note: The board could not read a price from Tronex Energy in the latest scan, and our scraper did not say why. That is our side, not theirs.
platforms.terms_source: Their pricing API accepts 1h, 1d, 3d and 7d and rejects everything else, so there is no ten-day rental to price: api.tronex.energy
platforms.deal_model_source: Their documented method prices the order for you: POST /api/v1/precountOrder takes days and volume and returns price and total: tronex.gitbook.io/docs/api-documentation/api-v1/energy
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Their pages mention "screened pools" without naming or addressing any of them, which is marketing rather than evidence.

platforms.price_note: Our own shop. Quoted from the same public price file the shop's pages read, and sorted here on price like every other row.
platforms.deal_model_source: Our own shop. One announced price per hour, paid by transfer, no bidding.
platforms.energy_source_source: Our own shop. It buys energy from other platforms and resells it, which is why it is on the board on the same terms as everyone else.

platforms.price_note: Tronify's queryPreorderInfo bundles a fixed energy package into every quote (observed +64,400 energy, matching pledgeConfig treasureType/transfer). data.pledgeTrxNum is the rental fee, not a refundable stake: it equals quoted_energy * orderPrice(sun) / 1e6 * days exactly. Prices here are the fee rescaled from the quoted energy to the board's 65k / 130k volumes.
platforms.terms_source: Their order API takes pledgeMinute 10, pledgeHour 1 or 3, and pledgeDay 1 to 30 — ten days is a valid day count, fifteen minutes is not a valid minute one: docs-tron.en.tronify.io
platforms.deal_model_source: Their order method carries an orderPrice the buyer sets, inside a floor and ceiling the platform publishes, and a seller closes that specific order. A fixed-price instant mode runs beside it: docs-tron.en.tronify.io/tron-api/create-trx-energy-order
platforms.energy_source_source: They publish a seller API with a staking threshold and pay sellers directly; the delegation transaction is signed by the seller, not by the platform: docs-tron.en.tronify.io/faq/tronify-faq

platforms.price_note: TronMax is an order book, not a shop: the buyer names the price and a seller fills it. These are the lowest prices TronMax will accept an order at - its own form rejects anything below them - so they are a floor, not a quote. Its public order list shows orders filling at exactly that floor. The rate is per day and rentals shorter than a day are billed as one, so fifteen minutes costs the same as a day at the same rate.
platforms.deal_model_source: The buyer types a price and their own form rejects anything under the per-duration minimum; their public order list shows what actually filled: api.tronmax.io/order/orders
platforms.energy_source_source: Their availability feed lists supply at each seller's rate and caps a single seller, so the energy comes from many independent sellers: api.tronmax.io/Setting/resource-available

platforms.price_note: These are TronSave's own order estimates, asked the way their checkout asks them: one call per amount and term. Their terms of service say the service is not offered in the United States or Vietnam.
platforms.deal_model_source: Their own documentation calls the price a bid and sorts the market by it: the buy endpoint takes a unitPrice, and SLOW / MEDIUM / FAST are how fast a seller is expected to take it (docs.tronsave.io/concepts/order-types).
platforms.energy_source_unknown: Their order book is behind an API key, so we cannot see who supplies the energy. The price endpoint answers without one, but it only quotes a total.

platforms.terms_source: Their API documentation states: 'Duration in hours. Currently only 1 hour is supported for energy, bandwidth, and resource_bundle.': docs.tronzap.com/api/transaction-create.html
platforms.deal_model_source: Their services endpoint publishes prices and the order call takes address, amount and duration with no price field: docs.tronzap.com/api/services.html
platforms.energy_source_unknown: They describe working with trusted stakers only in a forum reply we could not open directly, so we leave it unstated.
